also.title: What was left, with and without the payment

paragraphs.text: A **transfer** moves budget from one line to another; no money leaves, and the School Committee votes each one. A **reclass** moves a cost already paid from one fund to another. A **payment** sends money to a vendor, on a warrant.
The 30 June entry is a payment. It was charged to a line that had already spent past its budget, and was covered, inside the school total, by other lines’ leftovers.

so.text: FY2025 took in the most and FY2026 paid almost nothing from it until the 29 June re-charge. That it was spent before receipts expired fits, as a hypothesis.

spec.title: The circuit breaker fund, in and out

paragraphs.text: **4 February 2026, School Committee.** Prepaying special education tuition named as a use for a large year-end leftover; an open conversation called for if leftover is spent before it reaches free cash. (recording)
**24 June 2026, School Committee.** Four line-item transfers and the carry-forward orders voted; no tuition payment among them. (minutes, recording)
**29 June 2026, Journal.** Collaborative tuition the general fund had paid charged to the circuit breaker instead. (journal 2026/12/000692)
**30 June 2026, Journal.** Nine FLLAC invoices numbered for FY2027 paid from the general fund, check 218995. (journal 2026/12/001152)
**29 July 2026, School Committee.** Told FY2026 would close well below the year before. (minutes)
**22 October 2026, Finance Committee.** Prepaying a first quarter from circuit breaker money explained as a rule; this payment not mentioned. (recording)

**Allowed.** State law lets a school committee approve paying up to three months of tuition in advance (G.L. c. 71, s. 71D), and the state’s Division of Local Services uses this case as its example: a July to September bill, due 30 June, charged to the year that is ending.

**Not announced.** Every June and July 2026 meeting of the School Committee, Finance Committee and Select Board was read, minutes and recordings. None mentions this payment or the re-charge to the circuit breaker. No minutes record an advance-tuition vote, or a warrant covering the last two weeks of June.

**Not yet held.** The signed warrant, FLLAC’s invoices with their service dates, and the School Committee’s September year-end budget reviews. Each is a registered gap, listed on What we cannot answer.
